name: google-shopping/search
description: Search Google Shopping by keyword: product title, price, old price, store, rating, reviews, delivery and product ID, with price, sort and location filters.

q.description: The query you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Shopping search. This parameter is optional if using `shoprs` parameter.

gl.description: The country to use for the Google search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France) Head to the Google Shopping countries for a full list of supported Google Shopping countries.

hl.description: The language to use for the Google Shopping search. It's a two or three-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French), optionally followed by a two-letter or three-digit region code (e.g., `en-gb` for British English, or `es-419` for Latin American Spanish).

safe.description: The level of filtering for adult content. It can be set to `active` or `off`, by default Google will omit explicit content.

uule.description: The Google encoded location you want to use for the search. `uule` and `location` parameters can't be used together. For consistent results with coordinates-based `uule` parameter, a matching `gl` parameter is required. Head to UULE Generator if you need to convert a location or GPS coordinates to `uule` parameter, and vice versa.

start.description: Intended to define the result offset for pagination. Google Shopping's current layout does not support offset pagination: the `start` parameter is ignored and every request returns the first page of results (around 40 items). The `num` parameter is still accepted and forwarded to Google, but the current layout returns a fixed page size, so it does not change the number of results returned.

device.description: The device to use to get the results. It can be set to `desktop` (default) to use a regular browser, `tablet` to use a tablet browser (currently using iPads), or `mobile` to use a mobile browser.

shoprs.description: The parameter defines the token that includes metadata about query and search filter(s). Providing `q` parameter alongside the `shoprs` is **not** required. To apply multiple filters join them with `||` separator, e.g. `shoprs_1||shoprs_2||shoprs_3`.

on_sale.description: Show only products that are on sale. This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

sort_by.description: The sorting order of the results. Available options: `1` - Price: low to high `2` - Price: high to low This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

max_price.description: Upper bound of price range query. This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

min_price.description: Lower bound of price range query. This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

free_shipping.description: Show only products with free shipping. This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

google_domain.description: The Google domain to use. It defaults to `google.com`. Head to the Google domains for a full list of supported Google domains.

small_business.description: Show only products from small business. This parameter overrides corresponding filter embedded into `shoprs` parameter.

json_restrictor.description: The fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.

# Google Shopping Search

Returns Google Shopping results for a keyword search. Each product has a title, price, old price, store, rating, review count, delivery note and product ID. The only required input is the search text in `q`.

## Use cases

- Track the price and old price of competing products for a keyword such as `wireless earbuds`.
- Build a list of the cheapest or best rated products in a category using `sort_by`, `min_price` and `max_price`.
- Compare which stores list the same type of product and which ones offer free delivery.
- Collect product IDs and page tokens to fetch full product details in a second call.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/google-shopping/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"q": "wireless earbuds"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data`.

## Response fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `shopping_results[].title` | Product name as shown in the listing. |
| `shopping_results[].price / shopping_results[].extracted_price` | Current price as display text (for example `$14.99`) and as a number (`14.99`). |
| `shopping_results[].old_price / shopping_results[].extracted_old_price` | Previous or usual price, as text and as a number. Present only when the listing shows a discount. |
| `shopping_results[].source` | Name of the store that lists the product, for example `Target`. |
| `shopping_results[].rating / shopping_results[].reviews` | Average star rating and number of reviews for the product. |
| `shopping_results[].delivery` | Delivery note such as `Free delivery`. Not every item has it. |
| `shopping_results[].product_id` | Google Shopping catalog ID of the product. |
| `shopping_results[].serpapi_product_api.queryParams.page_token` | Token that identifies the product. Use it to request more details about the item. |
| `categorized_shopping_results[].title` | Name of a result group, for example `Best Overall Wireless Earbuds`. |
| `filters[].options[].shoprs` | Token for a ready-made filter such as `On sale` or `Under $35`. Pass it in the `shoprs` parameter to apply that filter. |

## Notes

- `q` is the only required parameter. Use `min_price`, `max_price`, `on_sale`, `free_shipping` and `sort_by` (`1` low to high, `2` high to low) to narrow the results.
- Pagination does not work. The `start` parameter is ignored and each request returns the first page of results.
- Take `page_token` from a result and call [Google Shopping Product Details](/apis/google-shopping/product) to get more information about one product.
- Some items have no `rating`, `reviews` or `product_id`, mostly those in `categorized_shopping_results`, so check for missing keys.

## Pricing

$0.015 per successful call. Failed calls are not charged. It is included in the daily free quota of each organization.
